description:
Runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and other terminal coding agents together on one mission.

Runner is a native desktop application where terminal agents work together. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Grok Build, Antigravity CLI, Copilot CLI and pi can take the same task in one mission, and each agent keeps its own TUI in a real terminal while the lead brings the decisions back to you. Everything in Runner is also a `runner` command: missions, crews, roles, projects, chats, sessions and messages are all addressable from the command line, with `runnerd` as the background service. Agents run natively on Windows without WSL, and PowerShell 7 is optional. Status: alpha, actively shipping. Native builds target macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64) on Windows 10 version 1809 or later; Intel Macs, Windows ARM64 and Linux are not supported. The installer, the application and the CLI sidecars are Authenticode-signed with a Certum open-source certificate issued to Open Source Developer Yicheng Wang.
Runner 0.18.2 is a feature release for macOS, Windows and Linux on top of 0.18.1. It brings Runner to Linux as a beta.
New
- Linux beta. Runner now runs natively on Linux ARM64 and x86_64, with signed .deb and tarball packages. Settings → Updates verifies and installs new versions in place, and an opt-in systemd user service keeps runnerd running without the app. This is a beta: it has been tried on an Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64 virtual machine, while native hardware, x86_64 and other distributions are not yet verified. Please report what you find. (#823)
Bug fixes
- Cancel restores Sign in. Pressing Cancel while signing in under Settings → Remote access now makes Sign in available again immediately. The abandoned attempt neither opens a browser nor interferes with a new sign-in, including one started in another window. (#1036, #1040)
- Remote access errors show up right away. When remote access cannot start, signing in or out now reports the actual error on the Remote access card at once instead of waiting about 45 seconds. (#1036)
Nightly channel
- Linux nightlies are published on the shared nightly prerelease alongside macOS and Windows, named Runner_nightly.<sha>.<stamp>_linux-<arm64|x64>.deb or .tar.gz so they appear after the macOS and Windows downloads. Linux nightly installs from before the rename do not see the renamed packages; reinstall once from the nightly page.
